title: Reconcile Project Members (.dpr/.dproj)
summary: Lists every unit a project uses that is neither a project member nor in the library, judges each one (project unit or third-party) and fixes it either way
intro: Read this after moving or adding units by hand, or when lint reports unit-not-in-dpr or unit-not-in-library. It lists every unit the project compiles that is neither in the .dpr/.dproj nor in the library, judges each by the project's own roots (inside = a missed project unit, outside = third-party), and offers two fixes: --apply adds the unit to the project (the default), --apply --to library adds its folder to the library. Without --apply it only reports.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Reconcile Project Members (.dpr/.dproj)...
steps: Open the project in RAD Studio
Choose drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Reconcile Project Members (.dpr/.dproj)...
Read the MISSING list: each unit is marked [project unit -> --apply] or [third-party -> library: --apply --to library]; units already in the library are not listed
Copy a command from SUGGESTED FIXES -- each is pre-narrowed with --only to the units its fix suits; nothing is written until you apply

surfaces.usage: drag-lint reconcile-project <App.dpr|.dproj> [--apply] [--to project|library] [--only <unit,...>] [--db <db>] [--full] [--json] [--config <path>] - sync project member list; flag stale used units. --only restricts MISSING (and therefore --apply) to a reviewed selection, so a dry run with --only previews exactly what --apply would write. --json carries `applied` (the OUTCOME, false when --apply had nothing to write) plus `backups` and `edited` when --apply is passed. MISSING = used units neither listed nor in the library (registry library path or the manifest library section's include); each is judged by the project's own roots: project unit (fix --apply) or third-party (fix --apply --to library, which adds its folder to that include in --config or the exe-dir drag-lint.json, .bak first). --json items carry owner, suggestedFix and folder
help: drag-lint reconcile-project <App.dpr|.dproj> [--apply] [--to project|library] [--only <unit,...>] [--db <db>] [--full] [--json] [--config <path>]  - sync project member list; flag stale used units. --only restricts MISSING (and therefore --apply) to a reviewed selection, so a dry run with --only previews exactly what --apply would write. --json carries `applied` (the OUTCOME, false when --apply had nothing to write) plus `backups` and `edited` when --apply is passed. MISSING = used units neither listed nor in the library (registry library path or the manifest library section's include); each is judged by the project's own roots: project unit (fix --apply) or third-party (fix --apply --to library, which adds its folder to that include in --config or the exe-dir drag-lint.json, .bak first). --json items carry owner, suggestedFix and folder
--db heals the index+findings for every project member (re-scan + recompile) WITHOUT editing the .dpr; --full forces the recompile even when nothing is incoherent
